summary: Global government investment in space defense has reached $71.8 billion as the militarization of space accelerates, coinciding with a new agreement between two European companies to study the concept of dropping missiles from orbit. In commercial space regulatory news, the Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for orbital data centers—an infrastructure setup that research indicates will require autonomous robots rather than astronauts for orbital maintenance. On the civil spacefront, Artemis III astronaut Andre Douglas visited NASA’s Vehicle Assembly Building to inspect the spacecraft designated for the upcoming crewed lunar landing mission. In commercial launch developments, Rocket Lab completed a record-setting Thanksgiving Day liftoff to successfully deliver a Japanese satellite into orbit. Major scientific achievements were also reported, including the discovery of a record-setting quasar formed just 630 million years after the Big Bang, as well as observations from the Hera spacecraft revealing a stadium-sized impact crater carved into an asteroid by a previous spacecraft collision. Looking ahead, readers should watch for NASA’s upcoming Cygnus NG-25 resupply mission, which will launch pioneering crop research to evaluate fresh produce for future lunar and Martian habitats.
